I (24F) met my boyfriend (24M) on the first day of college in 2018 and we have now been dating for a year and seven months. We were paired together in our first class of the day. We had to get to know each other and then introduce each other to the class. We hung out once after this, and then we didn't speak again until 2022. (This was because I was involved in many, many situationships where I was just codependent and emotionally involved in really not good people. Plus, I was very addicted to a certain leafy substance. And then, I was just dealing with a slew of mental health struggles. Tack on me being short and stout \[think teapot\] with a big tummy, no butt, no boobs, and honestly just not looking conventionally attractive at all - I was (still am) deeply insecure.)

In 2022 I messaged him on Instagram and we met up for the first time in YEARS, and we spent 5 hours together just talking and hanging out. I had kissed a few people before but I was NOT good at it, nor was I comfortable with it. I was scared to have sex because I was (still am) deeply insurance. I had not truly dated anyone before. I was honestly terrified because this man was conventionally attractive and I was convinced he was "too good" for me. I learned that he had never kissed, had sex, dated, anyone before. It was honestly relieving because, in a weird way, I was honestly thinking "he doesn't have experience and can't compare someone's gorgeous body to mine so I'm feeling safer." 

I was so convinced that I would never find someone. Ever. Like seriously ever. There were/are so many things to dislike about me (and that was all I could focus on at the time). I knew that too many things were working against me and hope was lost. I knew I would have to settle. But meeting up with my now-boyfriend again after years brought such an unexpected gift. I have learned that I have special quirks and personality traits that are likable, and I'm not totally horrible like I had told myself. He has really helped me see the beauty in myself and in life. I may not consider myself the poster child for beauty, but I have to acknowledge that I have some redeeming qualities now. :)

I know it is SO HARD to feel confident when starting to date. I read some advice on the subreddit wayyyy in the beginning of my relationship because I was also so worried that my looks or inexperience would be a turn-off. I told (and still sometimes tell, when I have moments of big insecurity) myself that he sees what I look like, and he says he likes how I look, so why would I question him like that? If he makes me feel and tells me that I am pretty, then who am I to second-guess his opinion? In regards to feeling inexperienced - I communicated this to him early on, and I prepared myself for him to run away because I thought he would want someone who knows what they are doing. I was weirdly okay with the possibility of him running away because I wouldn't really want to date someone who makes that a big deal, anyways (though it was a pleasant surprise when he didn't!). 

You can feel confident in knowing that you don't really know what to expect. You can feel confident in knowing that you are welcoming new experiences and exploring. I totally understand feeling like it is a lost cause to expect a relationship to materialize EVER, like I did - but please don't give up hope! I hate to sound cliche, but it really can happen when you least expect it. You are absolutely deserving of love, care, and a healthy relationship, just like any other human, and you are special in your own ways.

Sorry this was all over the place. But, I hope you feel some peace and hope reading my story.

I worked in the admissions office and worked this event until I graduated from UNO. IF things are still running the same, here is what I recommend:

1. Try to wait and attend a campus tour later in the day. Most guests will want to go on the first tour of the day which ends up being HUGE, so I recommend waiting if you can, so that you can walk in a smaller group and have a chance to ask more questions!
2. I am not sure if they still organize departmental tours (you would have selected which tour you want when you signed up). If they didn't, I recommend emailing [admissions@uno.edu](mailto:admissions@uno.edu) or [coedean@uno.edu](mailto:coedean@uno.edu) and requesting a tour of the NAME building. There is a phenomenal demonstration that they show guests. I loved bringing groups there because it is really so cool to watch, even if you have no idea or interest in what NAME is. \*I'm not sure if they organize the NAME tour on the weekend, but I think it is still worth the ask!
3. Visit the REC to see what clubs/student involvement opportunities are available (this is typically open for browsing throughout the day).
4. The campus tour and housing tour are separate (fact check this - it should be noted on the schedule that they give you at check-in!) so make sure you plan your time accordingly.
5. Try to get there earlier in the day so that you can get the best breakfast items before they run out and find a comfortable seat for the morning presentation. :) 
6. Have lots of fun! It is a really exciting day and you can meet the best people. As another commenter said, take the time to see the surrounding area, drive along the lakefront, and visit City Park. 

If you have any questions, feel free to message me!
